levels.title: Missing in adding and taking away

lesson.title: Undo it
lesson.body: To find ? in ? + 8 = 23, undo the adding: 23 − 8 = 15. Check by putting it back: 15 + 8 = 23.

lesson.title: Taking away
lesson.body: In 30 − ? = 18, ask what you take from 30 to leave 18: 30 − 18 = 12. In ? − 7 = 12, add the 7 back: 19.

lesson.title: Undo the times
lesson.body: ? × 6 = 42: undo the times by dividing, 42 ÷ 6 = 7. And ? ÷ 4 = 9: undo the dividing by multiplying, 9 × 4 = 36.

lesson.title: Check
lesson.body: Put your answer back in: 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so 36 is right.

lesson.title: A letter is a number
lesson.body: A letter stands for a number we do not know yet: in n + 7 = 20, n is 13. 4n means 4 × n.

lesson.title: Any letter
lesson.body: n, x or y: the letter does not matter. In 3y = 27, y = 9.

lesson.title: Undo in reverse
lesson.body: 2n + 3 = 17: undo the + 3 first, 17 − 3 = 14, then undo the × 2, 14 ÷ 2 = 7.

lesson.title: Follow the rule
lesson.body: A machine that multiplies by 3 and then adds 2 turns 4 into 4 × 3 + 2 = 14.

lesson.title: Running it backwards
lesson.body: If 14 came out, undo the steps in reverse: 14 − 2 = 12, then 12 ÷ 3 = 4 went in.

lesson.title: Find the step
lesson.body: In 4, 7, 10, 13, each number is 3 more than the one before, so the next is 16.

lesson.title: Count the steps
lesson.body: From the 1st number to the 20th there are 19 steps, not 20: the 20th number is 4 + 19 × 3.

templates.construct: Find a missing number in an addition by taking away

formats.prompt: Ana had some marbles. She was given {b} more and now has {c}. How many did she have at first?

hints: Undo the adding: take {b} away from {c}.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {b} to {c}. To undo + {b}, take {b} away.
{value} is the total. The missing number is {b} less than that.

templates.construct: Find how much was taken away

formats.prompt: There were {c} eggs. Some were used and {b} are left. How many were used?

hints: What do you take from {c} to leave {b}?

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {b} to {c}. Take {b} from {c} to find what was taken.
{value} is what is left. The question asks what was taken away.

templates.construct: Find the starting number of a taking away by adding back

formats.prompt: Lito spent ₱{a} and has ₱{b} left. How much did he have at first?

hints: Undo the taking away: add {a} back.

distractors.feedback: {value} is {b} − {a}. To undo − {a}, add {a} back.
{value} is what is left. The question asks what there was at first.

templates.construct: Find a missing factor by dividing

formats.prompt: {b} bags hold {c} sweets, the same number in each. How many sweets are in each bag?

distractors.feedback: {value} is {c} × {b}. To undo × {b}, divide by {b}.
{value} is {c} − {b}. To undo × {b}, divide by {b}.

templates.construct: Find the number something was divided by

formats.prompt: {c} pupils make {a} teams of the same size. How many pupils are in each team?

hints: What do you divide {c} by to get {a}?

distractors.feedback: {value} is {c} × {a}. Divide {c} by {a} to find the missing number.
{value} is the answer to the division. The question asks what {c} is divided by.

templates.construct: Find the number that was divided, by multiplying

formats.prompt: Some mangoes were shared equally among {b} families. Each family got {a}. How many mangoes were there?

distractors.feedback: {value} divides {a} by {b}. To undo ÷ {b}, multiply by {b}.
{value} is {a} + {b}. To undo ÷ {b}, multiply by {b}.

templates.construct: Solve a one-step equation with a letter: adding
hints: {L} stands for a number. Undo the + {b}.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {b} to {c}. To undo + {b}, take {b} away.
{value} is the total. {L} is {b} less than that.

templates.construct: Solve a one-step equation with a letter: multiplying, written 4n

distractors.feedback: {value} is {c} × {b}. To undo × {b}, divide by {b}.
{value} is {c} − {b}. {b}{L} means {b} × {L}, so divide by {b}.

templates.construct: Solve a one-step equation with a letter: dividing

distractors.feedback: {value} divides {a} by {b}. To undo ÷ {b}, multiply by {b}.
{value} is {a} + {b}. To undo ÷ {b}, multiply by {b}.

templates.construct: Solve a two-step equation by undoing the steps in reverse: times, then add

formats.prompt: I think of a number. I multiply it by {m}, then add {k}. I get {r}. What is my number?

hints: Undo the steps in reverse: first take away {k}, then divide by {m}.

distractors.feedback: {value} divides first. Undo the last step first: take away {k}, then divide by {m}.
{value} is {m} times the number. Divide by {m} too.
{value} adds {k}. To undo + {k}, take it away.

templates.construct: Solve a two-step equation by undoing the steps in reverse: times, then take away

formats.prompt: I think of a number. I multiply it by {m}, then take away {k}. I get {r}. What is my number?

hints: Undo the steps in reverse: first add {k} back, then divide by {m}.

distractors.feedback: {value} is {m} times the number. Divide by {m} too.
{value} takes {k} away. To undo − {k}, add it back.

templates.construct: Run a two-step number machine forwards

formats.prompt: A number machine multiplies by {m}, then adds {k}. What comes out when {x} goes in?

hints: Do the steps in order: first × {m}, then + {k}.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {k} first. The machine multiplies by {m} first, then adds.
{value} only multiplies. The machine adds {k} too.

templates.construct: Run a two-step number machine backwards

formats.prompt: A number machine multiplies by {m}, then takes away {k}. {r} comes out. What number went in?

hints: Run the machine backwards: undo the last step first.

distractors.feedback: {value} runs the machine forwards again. Undo the steps in reverse.
{value} undoes only the − {k}. Divide by {m} too.

templates.construct: Find the rule of a table and use it further on

formats.prompt: When x is 1, 2, 3 and 4, y is {m + k}, {2 * m + k}, {3 * m + k} and {4 * m + k}. What is y when x is {x}?

hints: How much does y go up each time x goes up by 1?
y goes up by {m} each time, and when x is 1, y is {m + k}.
steps: y goes up by {m}: the rule is {m} × x + {k}
templates.explain: The rule is y = {m} × x + {k}, so y = {m} × {x} + {k} = {answer}.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the next number in the table, for x = 5. Find the rule and use x = {x}.
{value} is {m} × {x}. The rule adds {k} too: check it with x = 1.

templates.construct: Continue a number pattern that goes up by the same step

formats.prompt: What comes next: {s}, {s + d}, {s + 2 * d}, {s + 3 * d}, … ?

hints: How much does the pattern go up each time?
Each number is {d} more than the one before.
steps: The last number shown is {s + 3 * d}
templates.explain: The pattern goes up by {d}: {s + 3 * d} + {d} = {answer}.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds 1. The pattern goes up by {d} each time.
{value} skips a number. The next one is only {d} more than {s + 3 * d}.

templates.construct: Find a missing number in the middle of a pattern

formats.prompt: What is the missing number: {s}, {s + d}, ?, {s + 3 * d}, {s + 4 * d}?

hints: Find the step from two numbers next to each other.
steps: The missing number is {d} more than {s + d}

distractors.feedback: {value} adds 1. The pattern goes up by {d} each time.
{value} is the number after the gap. The missing one is {d} less.

templates.construct: Find a far-off number in a pattern by counting the steps

formats.prompt: The pattern {s}, {s + d}, {s + 2 * d}, {s + 3 * d}, … goes on. What is the {n}th number?

hints: From the 1st number to the {n}th, how many steps of {d} are there?

distractors.feedback: {value} adds the step {n} times. From the 1st number to the {n}th there are only {n - 1} steps.
{value} is {n} × {d}. Start from the first number, {s}.

formats.prompt: What comes next: {s}, {2 * s}, {4 * s}, {8 * s}, … ?

hints: How does each number come from the one before?
Each number is double the one before.
steps: {2 * s} is double {s}, and {4 * s} is double {2 * s}
The last number shown is {8 * s}
templates.explain: Each number doubles: double {8 * s} is {answer}.

distractors.feedback: {value} adds {4 * s} again. Each number is double the one before, not the same step more.
{value} adds 1. Each number is double the one before.
